570836.long_answer: Thymomas almost always remain confined to the mediastinum or spread locally to pleura and pericardium. Hematogenous distant metastasis (stage IVb) occurs in only about 3–5 % of thymoma cases, and among those few, bone involvement has been reported almost exclusively in isolated case reports. Therefore, the probability of a thymoma metastasizing to bone is considered extremely rare—well under 5 % of all thymoma presentations.

996123.long_answer: In Birt–Hogg–Dubé syndrome, the skin lesions are confirmed as fibrofolliculomas by routine histopathology. A punch or shave biopsy processed with standard hematoxylin–eosin (H&E) staining demonstrates the hallmark features—cystically dilated follicular infundibula with thin epithelial strands radiating into a perifollicular fibrous stroma—thereby confirming the presence of fibrofolliculomas.

340619.long_answer: In heterozygous females, X-inactivation is usually random, but if it is skewed so that the X chromosome carrying the pathogenic mutation is preferentially inactivated, far fewer cells express the mutant gene. This lowers the overall burden of dysfunctional protein, resulting in a markedly milder (or even subclinical) manifestation of an X-linked dominant disorder; conversely, skewing toward inactivation of the normal X makes disease more severe. Thus, the direction of skewed X-inactivation modulates phenotypic severity.

488177.long_answer: Infliximab is a monoclonal antibody that neutralizes tumor-necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). It has been reported to control inflammation and bone lesions in chronic recurrent multifocal osteomyelitis and is an FDA-approved biologic for inducing and maintaining remission in Crohn’s disease, underscoring its therapeutic role in both conditions.

759868.long_answer: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans, a malignant fibro-histiocytic skin tumor that can be mistaken for a benign dermatofibroma, characteristically shows strong, diffuse immunohistochemical positivity for the cell-surface marker CD34, whereas ordinary dermatofibromas are CD34-negative. Therefore, CD34 staining is used to identify and confirm the malignant lesion.

390551.long_answer: Primary (congenital) empty sella syndrome results from a developmental defect of the diaphragma sellae. After a traumatic brain injury, cerebrospinal-fluid pulsations can herniate the subarachnoid space into the sella turcica, compressing the pituitary gland and producing hypopituitarism.

492729.long_answer: Both leukemia and COVID-19 frequently lead to thrombocytopenia—a reduction in circulating platelets. In leukemia, malignant infiltration of the bone marrow suppresses normal megakaryocyte function, lowering platelet production. In COVID-19, platelets are depleted by inflammatory consumption, immune-mediated destruction, and marrow suppression from systemic infection. The shared outcome of these distinct mechanisms is a clinically significant drop in platelet count, i.e., thrombocytopenia.

676444.long_answer: APMPPE is usually self-limited, and in most series 80–90 % of affected eyes regain visual acuity of 20/40 or better—often reaching 20/25-20/20—within weeks to a few months after the acute episode.

564619.long_answer: Loose anagen syndrome has been repeatedly described in patients with Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). NF1 is an autosomal-dominant RAS-pathway disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the NF1 gene and is classically characterized by multiple neurofibromas and other tumors of the nervous system (e.g., optic pathway gliomas, malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors). Several case reports and series document that children with NF1 can present with easily pluckable, sparse hair typical of loose anagen syndrome, linking this hair abnormality to the neurocutaneous tumor-predisposition condition NF1.

740626.long_answer: Pathogenic variants in CHMP2B (charged multivesicular-body protein 2B) are a recognised cause of autosomal-dominant hereditary spastic paraplegia (designated SPG82) and were originally identified in families with frontotemporal dementia (FTD3). Thus, the same CHMP2B mutations can underlie both hereditary spastic paraplegia and frontotemporal dementia through disruption of the ESCRT-III endosomal sorting pathway.

406351.long_answer: Congenital self-healing reticulohistiocytosis (Hashimoto-Pritzker disease) is a form of Langerhans cell histiocytosis. The disorder is characterized by proliferation of epidermal Langerhans cells, which are antigen-presenting dendritic cells integral to T-lymphocyte–driven (cell-mediated) immune reactions. Hence, the pathogenesis and lesion regression in this condition primarily involve a cell-mediated immune response rather than an antibody-mediated one.

376478.long_answer: Agonal respiration—irregular, gasping breaths that occur when the brainstem is transiently active despite loss of effective circulation—is commonly seen in the first minutes of cardiac arrest. These gasps signal severe cardiovascular collapse and impending respiratory system failure, indicating that the patient is in true cardiac arrest and requires immediate resuscitation.

887667.long_answer: FACES syndrome is a rare multiple-congenital-anomaly syndrome present from birth and thought to follow autosomal-recessive inheritance. Because it results from underlying genetic causes rather than environmental or purely developmental factors, it is classified as a genetic disorder.

126723.long_answer: Cross syndrome, also called oculocerebral hypopigmentation (Cross type), is characterized by generalized hypopigmentation of the skin and hair together with ocular and neurologic defects. Because it results from inherited defects in melanin biosynthesis, it is classed as a variant of oculocutaneous albinism, an autosomal-recessive genodermatosis.
